# remoc.rs

> Three Rust libraries for communication between programs: Remoc provides Rust RPC
> whose calls can pass typed channels and remote objects over a single connection;
> Aggligator combines multiple network links into one resilient
> connection; Postbag is a compact binary Serde codec with built-in schema
> evolution.

All three are Apache 2.0-licensed open source, written in 100% safe Rust and
built on Tokio.

## Remoc

- [Overview](https://remoc.rs/): Rust RPC where calls can pass typed channels and
  remote objects that remain usable after they return, all over one connection.
- [Channels between processes and machines](https://remoc.rs/remote-channels.html):
  mpsc, oneshot, watch and broadcast channels with the API known from Tokio,
  working over a network connection, socket or pipe.
- [IPC between Rust processes](https://remoc.rs/ipc.html): typed channels and
  trait calls between a daemon and its clients over a UNIX socket, a pipe to a
  child process or local TCP.
- [Server push and callbacks](https://remoc.rs/server-push.html): calls that
  return or accept channels, and clients that serve traits of their own, so the
  server can push events and call back through NAT.
- [Erlang-style message passing](https://remoc.rs/erlang-messaging.html):
  distributed Erlang's model of sending messages and addresses between machines,
  with typed messages and bounded channels; what OTP has that Remoc does not.
- [Multiplexing typed channels](https://remoc.rs/multiplexing.html): many
  independent, typed channels over one TCP, TLS or WebSocket connection, with
  per-channel flow control.
- [Comparison with other RPC libraries](https://remoc.rs/comparison.html): how
  Remoc differs from tarpc, gRPC (tonic) and Cap'n Proto.
- [Benchmarks](https://remoc.rs/benchmarks.html): throughput of a Remoc channel
  compared with plain TCP.
- [Examples](https://remoc.rs/examples/channels.html): remote channels, remote
  trait calls, distributed tracing and a web browser endpoint.
- [API documentation](https://docs.rs/remoc)

## Aggligator

- [Overview](https://remoc.rs/aggligator/): combines network links (TCP,
  WebSocket, USB, Bluetooth) between two endpoints into one connection with
  their combined bandwidth.
- [Keeping connections alive while switching networks](https://remoc.rs/aggligator/network-switching.html):
  a connection that survives a device moving between Wi-Fi, mobile data and
  Ethernet, even when its IP address changes.
- [Combining multiple internet connections](https://remoc.rs/aggligator/bonding.html):
  link bonding in user space, without Multipath TCP or special routers.
- [agg-tunnel](https://remoc.rs/aggligator/tunnel.html): forward TCP ports of
  existing, unmodified applications over an aggregated connection.
- [API documentation](https://docs.rs/aggligator)

## Postbag

- [Overview](https://remoc.rs/postbag/): a binary Serde format that lets your
  types keep changing.
- [Schema evolution](https://remoc.rs/postbag/schema-evolution.html): why binary
  formats like bincode break when types change and how Postbag allows fields and
  enum variants to be added, removed and reordered.
- [File formats](https://remoc.rs/postbag/file-formats.html): config and save
  files that stay readable across application versions, in both directions and
  without migration code. Recoverable fields, unique to Postbag, confine an
  incompatible change to one field instead of losing the whole file.
- [API documentation](https://docs.rs/postbag)
